plain_english: Thus the variety of meditation, worship, and the like becomes effective in action: an embodied, divided deity, when invoked, can abandon its own enjoyments and act in an instant.
sanskrit_cite:
dhyeyapūjyādivaicitryam ittham arthakriyākaram /
mūrto bhinnaḥ samāhūto hitvā bhogān nijān kṣaṇāt // [AgMsv_1.1115]

plain_english: Saying 'O god, he comes' is fitting only within scriptural statements; but all this is truly fitting only as the nature of the formless and so forth.
sanskrit_cite:
deva etīti vārtaiṣā vacaneṣv eva śobhate /
amūrtādisvarūpatvaṃ sarvam etat tu yujyate // [AgMsv_1.1116]

plain_english: Indeed the self alone, being of that nature, appears just so through division; for this is the very nature of consciousness, and that alone is what appears.
sanskrit_cite:
ātmaiva hi tathābhūtas tathā bhāty eva bhedataḥ /
evaṃ svabhāva evaiṣa saṃvido yaḥ sa eva tu // [AgMsv_1.1117]

plain_english: In scripture the karmic impurity is defined as being seized by division; but in the practice of initiation and related rites, it is not regarded as an impurity.
sanskrit_cite:
bhedagrastatayā kārmo malaḥ śāstre nirūpyate /
dīkṣādikarmayoge tu na malatvaṃ pratāyate // [AgMsv_1.1118]

plain_english: For initiation is vowed to burning away the entire world of transmigration made of division; and in reality it is of the nature of that true consciousness.
sanskrit_cite:
sa hi bhedamayāśeṣasaṃsāradahanavrataḥ /
dīkṣā ca vastutas tādṛksatyasaṃvitsvarūpiṇī // [AgMsv_1.1119]

plain_english: Thus it is said in the supreme doctrine: one who knows in this way knows in truth; for in the yoga of realization, when the sphere of division is quieted, this is understood.
sanskrit_cite:
evaṃ yo veda tattvenety uktaṃ cānuttare naye /
evaṃ vijñānayoge hi śamite bhedagocare // [AgMsv_1.1120]

plain_english: The self alone is Śiva, the one reality—so what bondage is there, and what liberation? Yet this is taught for the sake of entry into the great consciousness of initiation.
sanskrit_cite:
ātmaiva śiva evaikaḥ ko bandhaḥ kā ca muktatā /
etaddīkṣāmahāsaṃvidpraveśāya tu bhaṇyate // [AgMsv_1.1121]

plain_english: This initiation, whose nature is action, is for the removal of karmic and other impurities, operating within actions that are driven by the fixed force fashioned by nature.
sanskrit_cite:
kriyāsvabhāvadīkṣāsau karmādimalahānaye /
svabhāvakḷptaniyatibalākṣipteṣu karmasu // [AgMsv_1.1122]

plain_english: Because his experience is brought about simultaneously through the power of mantra, the determinations belonging to breath, space, limited agency, and time are likewise brought into play.
sanskrit_cite:
bhogo 'sya yugapadyasmāt kriyate mantraśaktitaḥ /
tathā hi prāṇagā deśakalākālādhvaniścayāḥ // [AgMsv_1.1123]

plain_english: His births are unfolded from earth all the way up to Śiva, and right there he becomes subject to birth, experience, authority, and dissolution.
sanskrit_cite:
jātayo 'sya pratāyante dharaṇyādiśivāntataḥ /
tatraiva janmasaṃbhogādhikāralayabhājanam // [AgMsv_1.1124]

plain_english: Thus, having been arranged and elevated from one level and placed in another, initiation—through the mutual, non-conceptual meeting of a guru established in settled consciousness and a disciple of actionless mind—blocks all the powers of prior karma.
sanskrit_cite:
vidhāyotkṛṣyate tasmād anyatra ca vidhīyate /

itthaṃ guror niścitasaṃvidātmarūḍheś ca śiṣyasya paraspareṇa /
niṣkarmacetor acitaiva dīkṣā prākkarmaśaktīr akhilā ruṇaddhi // [AgMsv_1.1125]

plain_english: Even there, the series of rice, sesame, ghee, oblations, and so forth—fashioned according to Śaiva necessity—does not, even at a clear stage, make the expanse of obscurity rootless, because division still continues to operate.
sanskrit_cite:
tatrāpi taṇḍulatilājyacaruprabandha ityādi śaivaniyatipratibhārakḷptam /
tāvaty api sphuṭapade na niśāprapañco nirmūlatām upagato 'pi vibhedavṛtteḥ // [AgMsv_1.1126]

plain_english: Even within difference, this pure element destroys the merit that would cause future transmigration. For that reason, the entire network of principles is only twofold, divided into pure and other.
sanskrit_cite:
bhede 'pi kiṃtv eṣa punar bhaviṣyasaṃsārakārisukṛtādivighātahetuḥ /
śuddhas tatas tad ata eva hi tattvajālaṃ śuddhetarasthititayā nikhilaṃ dvidhaiva // [AgMsv_1.1127]

plain_english: The pure reality shines as filled with the three powers and as paired. From this, ritual action is conceived in many ways, and so an expanse of restriction arises that brings about limited forms of enjoyment.
sanskrit_cite:
śuddhaṃ triśaktikhacitaṃ nanu yāmalaṃ ca bhāty eva tena bahudhaiṣa kṛtaḥ kriyāyāḥ /
vyāpārakalpanāvaśān niyatiprapañcaḥ svalpetaratvakṛtatādṛśabhogayogaḥ // [AgMsv_1.1128]

plain_english: Where the assemblage of seals and mandalas is practiced together with mantras and tantras, all practices such as yoga become capable of yielding their fruits.
sanskrit_cite:
mudrāmaṇḍalasaṃghātaḥ samantratantracarcitaḥ /
yatra yogādikaṃ sarvaṃ phaladānāya kalpate // [AgMsv_1.1129]

plain_english: Those who are fixed in the narrowed desire to attain liberation regard unlimitedness itself as the fruit to be obtained here.
sanskrit_cite:
nirvṛtiphalasaṃprāptikāṅkṣāsaṃkocasusthitāḥ /
anavacchinnatām eva phalatvenātra manvate // [AgMsv_1.1130]

plain_english: In what is unlimited and unbroken, there is no room for conceiving sacrifice and similar rites; such is the view of those who have transcended all that. Still, even when the supremely nondual reality is known, some desire for a fruit can remain.
sanskrit_cite:
na hy anantānav/yacchede kāpi yāgādikalpanā anavacchinnavāñchā // 1.1131 //

tatsarvottīrṇadṛṣṭayaḥ /
tathāpi vidite hy arthe paramādvayasundare // [AgMsv_1.1132]

plain_english: Because consciousness is free by its very nature, some people still desire fruits. For their sake, the entire teaching is set forth, from earth up to Śiva, so that their aims may be fulfilled.
sanskrit_cite:
saṃvitsvabhāvasvātantryāt keṣāṃcit phalakāmatā /
tāny evoddiśya tat sarvaṃ pūraṇāya dharāditaḥ // [AgMsv_1.1133]

plain_english: The teaching on concentrations sets out the whole range up to Śiva in many divisions. Here, unlike in other systems, nothing that appears is unreal; so for those who abide in truth, what could possibly fall into the category of what must be rejected?
sanskrit_cite:
śivāntaṃ bahudhā bhedair dhāraṇāgrantha ucyate

iha hi nānyanayeṣv iva kiñcana sphuritam asti na yat kila satyataḥ /
tad iha satyapade sthitibhāgināṃ kim iva heyapade nipatiṣyati // [AgMsv_1.1134]

plain_english: Thus the principle that appears as the culmination of the seventeen sections is determined to be the unsurpassed state of Śiva for those who desire attainment. Everything taught here appears in an opposing form, because this entire expanse stands animated by difference.
sanskrit_cite:
itthaṃ saptadaśādhikāracaramaṃ tattvaṃ yad ābhāsate tan nirṇītam anuttaraṃ śivapadaṃ saṃprāptikāmān prati /
etat sarvam ihoditaṃ ca jagadānande vipakṣātmakaṃ bhedaprāṇatayā yato 'tra nikhilo 'py eṣa prapañcaḥ sthitaḥ // [AgMsv_1.1135]

plain_english: Thus, in the second section, the great Lord is established as the self of all and is worshiped through gradual knowledge and yoga, and through concentrations.
sanskrit_cite:
dvitīyaḥ kāṇḍaḥ

evaṃ maheśvaro devo viśvātmatvena saṃsthitaḥ /
kramikajñānayogābhyāṃ dhāraṇābhir upāsyate // [AgMsv_2.1]

plain_english: In the eighteenth chapter, the sequence of principles is fully expounded as freed from the net of duality, impurity, māyā, and the like.
sanskrit_cite:
tattvakramaṃ gatadvaitamalamāyādijālakam /
aṣṭādaśe tat paṭale tattvaṃ samyag vibhāvyate // [AgMsv_2.2]

plain_english: Here, practices such as breath control are described as to be abandoned, because they are not a means to supreme knowledge.
sanskrit_cite:
prāṇāyāmādikaṃ yatra heyam ity eva varṇyate /
na hi tasya parāṃ vittiṃ prati kācid upāyatā // [AgMsv_2.3]

plain_english: What is firmly established within consciousness cannot be moved into the apparatus of breath and mind; so how could a method of practice make that happen? If some still strive to refine consciousness through practice, we doubt what they could accomplish, where, from what basis, and how.
sanskrit_cite:
antaḥ saṃvidi yan nirūḍham abhitas tat prāṇadhīvigrahe saṃcāryeta kathaṃ tatheti ghaṭatām abhyāsayogakramaḥ /
ye tv abhyāsapathena saṃvidam imāṃ saṃskartum abhyudyatās te kiṃ kutra kutaḥ kathaṃ vidadhatām ity atra saṃdihmahe // [AgMsv_2.4]

plain_english: Practice means doing something over and over again, and even that arises from differences of space and time and from involvement with appearance and otherness; so it takes place on the path of body, mind, breath, and senses.
sanskrit_cite:
abhyāso hi punaḥ punar arthaḥ so 'pi ca dikkālapratibhedāt /
ābhāsetarayogasamuttho dehamanaḥprāṇākṣapathe syāt // [AgMsv_2.5]

plain_english: Those who wish to enter the Bhairava form, which is dense with pure light alone, become firmly established simply by resting in knowledge that shines forth once.
sanskrit_cite:
prakāśaikaghane rūpe bhairavīye vivikṣavaḥ /
sakṛdvibhātavijñānaviśrāntyaiva susaṃsthitāḥ // [AgMsv_2.6]

plain_english: For that reason, concentration is declared here to be the supreme and universally helpful limb, and concentrations determined through that same door may become of that very nature.
sanskrit_cite:
atraivātaḥ paraṃ proktam aṅgaṃ sarvopakāri yat /
dhāraṇā api taddvāraniścitāḥ syus tathātmikāḥ // [AgMsv_2.7]

plain_english: But surely, what confidence can be placed in reasoning that has no firm ground? Or else, why would your own statement not be struck down by the same lack of ground?
sanskrit_cite:
nanv apratiṣṭhe kas tarke samāśvāsaḥ prakalpyatām /
kiṃ vā na bhavatāṃ tādṛg apratiṣṭhāhataṃ vacaḥ // [AgMsv_2.8]

plain_english: Likewise, if some insist that scripture alone is the valid means of knowledge, how is certainty to be reached when there is a whole host of scriptures that contradict it?
sanskrit_cite:
tathā hy āgama evaikaṃ pramāṇam iti niścitaiḥ /
tadviruddhāgamavrāte sati niścīyatāṃ katham // [AgMsv_2.9]

plain_english: But if acceptance by the great multitude is taken as the reason for validity, that too is ungrounded, because a great multitude opposed to it can just as well exist.
sanskrit_cite:
mahājanaprasiddhis tu tatra prāmāṇyakāraṇam /
apratiṣṭhā tadviruddhamahājanasusaṃbhavāt // [AgMsv_2.10]

plain_english: Even perception, in matters like taste and so on, is seen to be overruled, and it becomes subject to an endless regress of later cognitions, does it not?
sanskrit_cite:
pratyakṣam api rucyādau dṛṣṭabādhakasaṃvidam /
uttarottaravijñānānavasthābhājanaṃ nanu // [AgMsv_2.11]

plain_english: If even self-awareness were overruled in that way, how could this person, skilled in joining differences together, carry on any practical dealings at all?
sanskrit_cite:
svasaṃvid api tatraiva bādhiteti kathaṃ kila /
vyavahāram ayaṃ kuryād bhedasaṃdhānapaṇḍitaḥ // [AgMsv_2.12]

plain_english: But for us there can never be groundlessness at any time or place, because for us the supreme, all-full ocean of Bhairava is present everywhere.
sanskrit_cite:
asmākaṃ tv apratiṣṭhānaṃ na kadācit kvacid bhavet /
yeṣāṃ sarvatra saṃpūrṇaḥ paro bhairavasāgaraḥ // [AgMsv_2.13]

plain_english: Especially for those whose awareness has received the supreme nectar by crossing the ocean of reasoning, reasoning itself is not ungrounded.
sanskrit_cite:
viśeṣatas tu tarkasya tān praty evāpratiṣṭhatā /
ye tarkārṇavatārāttaparamāmṛtasaṃvidaḥ // [AgMsv_2.14]

plain_english: For all the parts of reasoning that do not touch self-awareness never, anywhere, attain Śiva as their final fruit.
sanskrit_cite:
tathā hi sarve tarkāṃśā anāmṛṣṭasvasaṃvidaḥ /
sarvatra paryantaphalaṃ na śivaṃ pratipedire // [AgMsv_2.15]

plain_english: The meaning of all scripture is essentially non-difference; any difference brought forth there is for attaining that non-difference, yet those of deluded intellect take delight in the difference itself.
sanskrit_cite:
abhedasāraḥ sarvo hi śāstrārthas tatprapattaye /
yas tatrodbhāvito bhedas tatra mūḍhadhiyo ratāḥ // [AgMsv_2.16]

plain_english: Reasoning is skilled only in cutting down the arguments of views based on difference; but surely, does reasoning have any usefulness even in the realm of non-difference?
sanskrit_cite:
tarkaś ca bhedavādāṃśayukticchedaikapaṇḍitaḥ /
nanv abhede 'pi tarkasya kā cid asty upayogitā // [AgMsv_2.17]

plain_english: In the vision of supreme nonduality, even reasoning is not truly fitting; therefore, for that supreme nonduality whose nature is grace to the universe, the text declares the Heart, whose nature is vibration, to be the supreme means.
sanskrit_cite:
paramādvayadṛṣṭau ca so 'pi naiva na saṃgataḥ /
ata eva parādvaitaṃ yad viśvānugrahātmakam /
tasyopāyaṃ paraṃ brūte hṛdayaṃ spandanātmakam // [AgMsv_2.18]

plain_english: In the Heart, which is made of awareness, there is a self-reflective awareness, the wonder of full consciousness, which all at once, suddenly and forcibly, dissolves the outward flashing of the universe.
sanskrit_cite:
hṛdaye bodhamaye yaḥ svavimarśaḥ pūrṇaciccamatkāraḥ /
yugapad drāgiti haṭhato līnīkṛtaviśvataḥsphuraṇaḥ // [AgMsv_2.19]

plain_english: In the first and last moments of grasping things, that state which is fully filled with surging bliss and made of the bliss of the whole world is called the universal vibration.
sanskrit_cite:
bhāvagrahādyacaramadaśāyor ullāsinirvṛtisupūrṇaḥ /
jagadānandamayo 'sau sāmānyaspanda ity uktaḥ // [AgMsv_2.20]

plain_english: The manifest flashing of the Heart, which shines forth as pure being from the abode of emission, leads one into the triad of powers to the very extent that it is recognized.
sanskrit_cite:
sphuraṇaṃ hṛdayasya yat kila prakaṭam idaṃ visargadhāmnaḥ /
sad iti pratibhāti yāvatā trikaśaktau viśatīha tāvatā // [AgMsv_2.21]

plain_english: This Heart is defined as the supreme nectar of Bhairava awareness, situated on the trident of the powers of will, knowledge, and action; from the supreme abode it is emitted.
sanskrit_cite:
tad idaṃ hṛdayaṃ nirucyate paramaṃ bhairavasaṃvidāmṛtam /
iṣidṛkkṛtiśaktiśūlagaṃ parame dhāmni visṛjyate tataḥ // [AgMsv_2.22]

plain_english: In the supreme, lordly Self this universe flashes forth as consciousness, situated on the trident of the three powers, and then proceeds by the path of emission on the Śāmbhava level.
sanskrit_cite:
parame bhagavatparātmani sphuritaṃ viśvam idaṃ cidātmakam /
śaktitrayaśūlagaṃ tataḥ śāmbhavabhūmivisargavartmanā // [AgMsv_2.23]

plain_english: That is then proclaimed as pure being; this full Heart, of the nature of 'I', always shines forth as the very flashing of the union of Śiva and Śakti.
sanskrit_cite:
tad atho sad iti pragīyate tad idaṃ pūrṇam ihāhamātmakaṃ /
hṛdayaṃ śivaśaktisaṃgamasphuraṇātmaiva sadāvabhāsate // [AgMsv_2.24]

plain_english: Here, in the Heart, sequences of creation, dissolution, and maintenance shine forth by the hundreds or even by thousands of millions, eternally, gathered through the agencies of Hara, Viṣṇu, and the lotus-born.
sanskrit_cite:
iha sṛṣṭilayasthitikramāḥ śataśo vāpi sahasrakoṭiśaḥ /
pravibhānti sadātanātmanā haraviṣṇvambujahetusaṃcitāḥ // [AgMsv_2.25]

plain_english: But for one who is not able to enter immediately through the collection of reasonings stated before, the vibration of the Heart is made manifest by the path of the śākta means.
sanskrit_cite:
iha tu puroktād yuktikalāpād yaḥ praviśet sadyo nāśaktaḥ /
taṃ prati śāktopāyapathena prakaṭīkriyate hṛdayaspandaḥ // [AgMsv_2.26]

plain_english: One reaches the path of the Heart by impelling the breath at the tip of the trident, and becomes intent on resting in the moon-digit of consciousness within that.
sanskrit_cite:
triśūlaprāntagaprāṇapreraṇāvāptahṛtpathaḥ /
tadantarvarticiccandrakalāviśrāntitatparaḥ // [AgMsv_2.27]

plain_english: Then, suddenly, by abandoning that level and casting off those states beginning with absence of bliss, which are situated amid the five elements, one moves beyond them.
sanskrit_cite:
jhaṭity evātha tadbhūmityāgena projjhya tā daśāḥ /
nirānandādikāḥ pañcabhūtamadhyavyavasthitāḥ // [AgMsv_2.28]

plain_english: Intent on complete rest, one should abandon the former stage and move to the higher one, because the ground of innate bliss follows upon the peaceful state.
sanskrit_cite:
tyajet pūrvāṃ parāṃ krāmet samyagviśrāntitatparaḥ /
yato nijānandamayī bhūmiḥ śāntapadānugā // [AgMsv_2.29]

plain_english: Nirānanda and parānanda, connected with puruṣa and the unborn, arise from the expansion of bliss produced by masses of undivided and divided objects of experience.
sanskrit_cite:
nirānandaparānandau puruṣājātasaṃgatau /
abhedabhinnabhogyaughajanitānandajṛmbhaṇāt // [AgMsv_2.30]

plain_english: A wondrous state of great bliss, of leftward course, shines forth in the great abode of Bhairava, in consciousness that has taken all within itself.
sanskrit_cite:
mahānandasthitiḥ kāpi vāmācārā samullaset /
bhairavīyamahādhāmni svīkṛtāśeṣasaṃvidi // [AgMsv_2.31]

plain_english: Great bliss, having become the bliss of consciousness, proceeds again in this triad that has taken in all the right, left, and upper aspects.
sanskrit_cite:
mahānandaś cidānandībhūya bhūyaḥ pravartate /
asmiṃs tu svīkṛtāśeṣadakṣavāmordhvagatrike // [AgMsv_2.32]

plain_english: In the triad whose nature is to grasp both duality and nonduality in every way, things may appear as undivided, or divided, or both divided and undivided.
sanskrit_cite:
trike sarvātmanā dvaitādvaitasaṃgrahaṇātmani /
abhinnā vātha bhinnā vā bhinnābhinnā athāpi vā // [AgMsv_2.33]

plain_english: Beings, joined with the five states of bliss beginning with innate bliss, arise from the state of intense, overflowing universal bliss.
sanskrit_cite:
bhāvā nijādikānandadaśāpañcakayojitāḥ /
jāyante jagadānandasamuddāmadaśājuṣaḥ // [AgMsv_2.34]

plain_english: Innate bliss is founded only on resting in the aspect of the subject, while the state of nirānanda arises from resting only in emptiness.
sanskrit_cite:
nijānandaḥ pramātraṃśamātraniṣṭhanibandhanaḥ /
śūnyatāmātraviśrānter nirānandātmikā sthitiḥ // [AgMsv_2.35]

plain_english: Supreme bliss also fully arises from resting in the domain of the object, when the object is filled on all sides with the collision of infinite knowables.
sanskrit_cite:
prameyapadaviśrānteḥ parānando 'py udety alam /
anantameyasaṃghaṭṭapūrṇe meye tu sarvataḥ // [AgMsv_2.36]

plain_english: The state called great bliss arises from the means of knowing through the yoking of savoring; it is skilled in devouring the apprehension of all masses of knowers and knowns.
sanskrit_cite:
pramāṇāc carvaṇāyogān mahānanda iti sthitiḥ /
samastamānameyaughakalanāgrāsakovidaḥ // [AgMsv_2.37]

plain_english: When one attains a rest that is unconditioned and utterly full, then indeed there is consciousness-bliss, which is not nourished by anything inert.
sanskrit_cite:
yadā viśrāntim abhyeti nirupādhisunirbharām /
tadā khalu cidānando yo jaḍānupabṛṃhitaḥ // [AgMsv_2.38]

plain_english: Where there is no divided state of inert form, where there is no division at all, and which shines forth on every side.
sanskrit_cite:
na ca yatra sthitiḥ kāpi vibhaktā jaḍarūpiṇī /
yatra ko 'pi vyavacchedo nāsti yad viśvataḥ sphurat // [AgMsv_2.39]

plain_english: Our teacher declared that very reality—unstruck awareness nourished by supreme nectar—to be the abode of universal bliss.
sanskrit_cite:
yad anāhṛtasaṃvitti paramāmṛtabṛṃhitam /
tad eva jagadānandadhāmāsmākaṃ gurur jagau // [AgMsv_2.40]

plain_english: Where contemplation and other practices have no primary applicability, rest should be established there through the yoga of utterance in the heart.
sanskrit_cite:
yatrāsti bhāvanādīnāṃ na mukhyā kāpi saṃgatiḥ /
tatra viśrāntir ādheyā hṛdayoccārayogataḥ // [AgMsv_2.41]

plain_english: The complete rest attained there is called supreme nonduality; it comes about through the application of the breath-staff and the equalizing of before and after.
sanskrit_cite:
yā tatra samyag viśrāntis tat parādvaitam ucyate /
prāṇadaṇḍaprayogena pūrvāparasamīkṛteḥ // [AgMsv_2.42]

plain_english: By the yogin, elsewhere than in the ordinary person’s division of bondage and liberation, the ground is sprinkled by the mansion of the pendant lotus tetrad.
sanskrit_cite:
catuṣkikāmbujālambilambikāsaudhasiktabhūḥ /
bandhamokṣavibhāgena narād anyatra yoginā // [AgMsv_2.43]

plain_english: By the unsurpassed nature that operates through the activity of speech, united with the dissolution and flourishing of the supreme I in the reflective awareness of consciousness.
sanskrit_cite:
anuttarasvabhāvena vāgvyāpārābhivartinā /
cidvimarśaparāhaṃkṛtpralayollāsayoginā // [AgMsv_2.44]

plain_english: When the entity is illuminated by the sun—emptied of effort and whose nature is the true twelve phases—it is filled and fully pervaded.
sanskrit_cite:
udyogavaśariktena saddvādaśakalātmanā /
sūryeṇābhāsite bhāve pūrite paricarcite // [AgMsv_2.45]

plain_english: Having entered the fire of awakening, the one possessing the sixteen named phases completely releases the phases, which are slowed by the power of devouring that.
sanskrit_cite:
tadgrāsamantharavaśāḥ ṣoḍaśākhyakalājuṣā /
praviṣṭeṇa vibodhāgnau samyag visṛjatā kalāḥ // [AgMsv_2.46]

plain_english: By the one who has internalized the infinite principles from ka to kṣa on all sides, whose state remains unchanged after attaining emission, the four life-giving powers are attained.
sanskrit_cite:
catasro jīvanīḥ prāptavisargāvikṛtasthiteḥ /
antaḥkṛtānantatattvakādikṣāntena sarvataḥ // [AgMsv_2.47]

plain_english: Joined to the heart where there is no reflection on the essence of the beingness of things, resting upon the eye of the yogin lineage fit for outward emission.
sanskrit_cite:
bhāvānāṃ bhāvatāsāravimarśābhāvahṛdyujā /
bahiḥprasavasadyogikulanetryadhiśāyinā // [AgMsv_2.48]

plain_english: By the state of Rudra-union, that stairway-garland of powers—ending in consciousness, breath, quality, and body—is always indeed established.
sanskrit_cite:
rudrayāmalabhāvena nityaṃ yā niṣṭhitaiva tām /
citprāṇaguṇadehāntaśaktisopānamālikām // [AgMsv_2.49]

plain_english: Then, having released through emission moving within the womb of vibration, one embraces the ground of emission, which enjoys the state of the fish-womb.
sanskrit_cite:
visargena visṛjyātha spandanodaravartinā /
visargabhūmim āśliṣya matsyodaradaśājuṣam // [AgMsv_2.50]

plain_english: Having ascended the ground of the trident, connected with the three channels, one reaches the supreme phase that is present in all, pervading all, and life-giving to all.
sanskrit_cite:
sarvasarvagatāṃ sarvajīvanīṃ paramāṃ kalām /
triśūlabhuvam ākramya nāḍītritayasaṃgatām // [AgMsv_2.51]

plain_english: One reaches the stairway-garland of powers ending in the brow-center, bindu, and nāda—expanding and contracting, and resorting in sequence to unity.
sanskrit_cite:
vikasvarāṃ saṃkucitāṃ krameṇaikātmyam āśritām /
bhrūkuṭībindunādāntaśaktisopānamālikām // [AgMsv_2.52]

plain_english: She contracts and expands like the alternating flow of a she-donkey and a mare, again and again full of streams of beings that dissolve and are created.
sanskrit_cite:
rāsabhīvaḍavāsrāvasasaṃkocavikāsikām /
muhur muhur līyamānasṛṣṭabhāvaughanirbharām // [AgMsv_2.53]

plain_english: She makes the great root spike into one emissive abode and rests in the heart of Bhairavī, who nourishes all beings.
sanskrit_cite:
ekīkṛtamahāmūlaśūlavaisargikāspadām /
samagrabhāvabharaṇabhairavīyahṛdāśritām // [AgMsv_2.54]

plain_english: This goddess, who has won the supreme name by boldly filling all, is without beginning or end and is inclined toward the whole universe.
sanskrit_cite:
sarvāpūraṇahevākasamarjitaparābhidhām /
ādyantarahitām enāṃ viśvapravaṇaśālinīm // [AgMsv_2.55]

plain_english: Having attained the goddess, the moonlight of the consciousness-moon in the space of heart-awareness and ruler of the triad, what indeed does one not obtain, and even cause others to obtain?
sanskrit_cite:
hṛdbodhākāśaciccandracandrikāṃ tritayeśikām /
devīṃ prāpya na kiṃ nāma labhate lambhyaty api // [AgMsv_2.56]

plain_english: Therefore, when the yogi, using means grounded in the contemplative body, wishes to enter the supreme, he first trembles.
sanskrit_cite:
tad atra bhāvanādehagatopāyaiḥ pare sati /
yadaiṣa pravivikṣuḥ syād yogī tāvad prakampate // [AgMsv_2.57]

plain_english: He trembles because, for hundreds of past births, he has been certain of identity with the body and has imagined consciousness and body to be one, like water mixed with dust.
sanskrit_cite:
pūrvajanmaśatābhyastadehatādātmyaniścayaḥ /
jalapāṃsuvad ekatvaṃ manvānaś ciccharīrayoḥ // [AgMsv_2.58]

plain_english: He may first enter the perfectly full conscious self, free from the māyā called difference, through the process of pressing forward by his own power.
sanskrit_cite:
bhedākhyamāyārahite paripūrṇacidātmani /
praviśet prathamaṃ yāvat svabalākramaṇakramāt // [AgMsv_2.59]

plain_english: For him there may arise a kind of sleep that loosens his immersion in the body, appearing just as trembling, so long as firm establishment in the supreme self has not yet arisen.
sanskrit_cite:
bhaven nidrāsya sā dehāveśaśaithilyadāyinī /
kamprarūpaiva yāvan no rūḍhir jātā parātmani // [AgMsv_2.60]

plain_english: This is the unmanifest sign, whose nature is man, power, and Śiva, in which this whole universe is dissolved and which is understood as present within.
sanskrit_cite:
etad avyaktaliṅgaṃ tannaraśaktiśivātmakam /
yatra viśvam idaṃ līnaṃ yad antaḥsthaṃ ca gamyate // [AgMsv_2.61]

plain_english: Moreover, this whole aggregate of paths has already been determined as present in the body; by the force of its unfolding, absorption may become clear.
sanskrit_cite:
kiṃ cādhvajātam etad dehasthatayaiva pūrvanirṇītam /
tasyonmeṣavaśena sphuṭatāṃ yāyāt samāveśaḥ // [AgMsv_2.62]

plain_english: When the mind-principle abides in a state of special vibration, consciousness-bliss arises from the fullness of Śakti's radiance, bearing within it the supreme essence of mantra-power.
sanskrit_cite:
cittattvasya viśeṣaspandadaśāśālinaś cidānandaḥ /
śāktasamullāsabharād antaḥkṛtamantravīryaparasāraḥ // [AgMsv_2.63]

plain_english: This sign, consisting of man and power and being both manifest and unmanifest, is said in scripture to blossom with the sap of the fruit of accomplishment.
sanskrit_cite:
naraśaktimayam idaṃ tadvyaktāvyaktaṃ bhavel liṅgaṃ /
siddhiphalaprasavarasaprasūnam iti kathyate śāstre // [AgMsv_2.64]

plain_english: But the manifest sign is said to be that which consists only of man; this threefold division is an arrangement of one single vibration.
sanskrit_cite:
vyaktaliṅgaṃ tad uktaṃ tu yat kevalanarātmakam /
ekasya spandanasyeyaṃ tridhā bhedavyavasthitiḥ // [AgMsv_2.65]

plain_english: Those whose hearts lack knowledge of this sign worship an external liṅga in vain; that is mere effort and cannot bring the true fruit.
sanskrit_cite:
etalliṅgajñānapraviyuktahṛdā vṛthaiva hi bhajante /
bāhyasthaliṅgapūjāṃ prayāsamātraṃ phalāya na hi tat syāt // [AgMsv_2.66]

plain_english: The manifest sign called the self-sign, resting on the human form, arises when the whole external universe is filled with non-difference from the body.
sanskrit_cite:
yad vyaktam ātmaliṅgākhyaṃ nararūpasamāśrayi /
dehābhedamaye bāhye viśvasmin bharite sati // [AgMsv_2.67]

plain_english: For the yogi absorbed on the level of great bliss, the primal sign therefore comes directly face-to-face.
sanskrit_cite:
samudeti mahānandabhūmau līnasya yoginaḥ /
tenādyaṃ liṅgam abhyeti saṃmukhīnatvam añjasā // [AgMsv_2.68]

plain_english: One should always abide in this sign, intent on resting in worship, for it is the heart of the yoginīs, the temple of supreme bliss.
sanskrit_cite:
atra liṅge sadā tiṣṭhet pūjāviśrāntitatparaḥ /
yadyoginīnāṃ hṛdayaṃ paramānandamandiram // [AgMsv_2.69]

plain_english: There, in the abodes of bliss of the previously taught seed, womb, parts, and emission, the wise gather an indescribable attainment of identity.
sanskrit_cite:
pūrvoktabījayonyaṃśavisargānandamandirāḥ /
yatra kāmapi tādātmyasampattiṃ cinvate budhāḥ // [AgMsv_2.70]

plain_english: There, without effort, the whole host of deities abides in the bliss-filled abode, their nature being eternally arisen consciousness.
sanskrit_cite:
yatra prayāsavirahāt sarvo 'sau devatāgaṇaḥ /
ānandapūrṇe dhāmny āste nityoditacidātmakaḥ // [AgMsv_2.71]

plain_english: That shining of Lord Bhairava as contraction and expansion appears even though, in truth, contraction and expansion are not present in him.
sanskrit_cite:
yattadbhairavanāthasya saṃkocetarabhāsanam /
avidyamānasaṃkocavikāsasyāpi bhāsate // [AgMsv_2.71]

plain_english: Sprinkled by that stream of bliss arising from the impact of consummation, this universe casts off its oldness.
sanskrit_cite:
yattatsamāptisaṃghaṭṭasamutthānandadhārayā /
avasiktam idaṃ viśvam apojjhati purāṇatām // [AgMsv_2.72]

plain_english: There, effortful striving as a task is misplaced, because what is ever risen like the sun does not need to be sought with a lamp.
sanskrit_cite:
tatra praveśane yatnaḥ kāryatvena prayāsakṛt /
yataḥ sadodito bhānuḥ kiṃ dīpena vicāryate // [AgMsv_2.73]

plain_english: Whether the yogi is established in his own self on the level of Śiva's conscious vibration, or delights the circle of yoginīs through special streams of external beings,
sanskrit_cite:
yadi svātmasthito yogī śivacitspandabhūmigaḥ /
yadi vā bāhyabhāvaughaviśeṣayoginīkulanandanaḥ // [AgMsv_2.74]

plain_english: Even in the absence of an object like a pot, that state consisting of the appearance of universal vibration is the supreme Bhairava seal, with inward focus and outward gaze.
sanskrit_cite:
ghaṭābhāve 'pi sāmānyaspandābhāsamayīṃ sthitim /
parabhairavamudrāṃ tām antarlakṣabahirdṛśam // [AgMsv_2.77]

plain_english: Then that supreme Śaiva goddess resorts again to the stream of phenomena, which is fashioned by the play of her freedom and consists of manifold efficacies.
sanskrit_cite:
yad āśrayati śaivī sā parā devī tataḥ punaḥ /
svātantryahelānirmeye tattadarthakriyāmaye // [AgMsv_2.78]

plain_english: In that stream of phenomena, joined to the savor of eager, awakening awareness, she touches Śakti—the true ground of particular vibration—and abides there.
sanskrit_cite:
bhāvaughe sotsukaunmukhyavimarśarasayogataḥ /
viśeṣaspandasadbhūmiṃ śaktiṃ saṃspṛśya vartate // [AgMsv_2.79]

plain_english: Presided over by this power, one's own mantras, in its manifestation, attain autonomy even in the midst of various accomplishments.
sanskrit_cite:
etenādhiṣṭhitā dhāmnā svamantrāstatprakāśane /
yānti svātantrayogitvaṃ vicitrāsvapi siddhiṣu // [AgMsv_2.80]

plain_english: Having become firmly established in a mode beyond rejection and acceptance, he sees everything shining forth, through its connection with all manifestation, as consciousness itself.
sanskrit_cite:
hānādānatiraskāravṛttau rūḍhim upāgataḥ /
sarvabhāsanayogena bhāsamānaṃ cidātmanā // [AgMsv_2.81]

plain_english: Seeing the visible from a stance of non-difference, through the wonder of consciousness, he abandons the timid state that comes from the wretched craving for practical results.
sanskrit_cite:
abhedavṛttitaḥ paśyan dṛśyaṃ citicamatkṛteḥ /
arthakriyārthitādainyakāritāṃ kātarāṃ sthitm // [AgMsv_2.82]

plain_english: Having abandoned that state, as long as he remains so, he effortlessly enters the Bhairava-like Śāmbhava level, the supreme state.
sanskrit_cite:
vihāya yāvad āsīta tāvac chāṃbhavabhūmikām /
bhairavīm āviśaty eva parāṃ bhūmim ayatnataḥ // [AgMsv_2.83]

plain_english: For one whose awareness is entered by this state, everything is seen as pervaded by the nature of light, for it is consciousness that shines.
sanskrit_cite:
etadāviṣṭasaṃvitti sarvam eva nirīkṣyate /
prakāśarūpatākrāntaṃ caitanyaṃ hi prakāśate // [AgMsv_2.84]

plain_english: And what is unmanifest does not attain manifestation merely by being connected with something to be manifested; this has already been explained at length.
sanskrit_cite:
na cāprakāśaṃ prākāśyayogād eti prakāśatām /
iti vistarataḥ pūrvaṃ prakāśitam idaṃ yataḥ // [AgMsv_2.85]

plain_english: All his activities dissolved through union with great audacity, his mind becomes wholly filled by a concentrated mass of his own rays.
sanskrit_cite:
mahāsāhasasaṃyogavilīnākhilavṛttikaḥ /
puñjībhūtasvaraśmyoghanirbharībhūtamānasaḥ // [AgMsv_2.86]

plain_english: Thinking of nothing and having abandoned the state of clearly seen difference, as long as he remains so, the previously described levels come forward.
sanskrit_cite:
akiṃciccintakaḥ spaṣṭadṛṣṭabhedojjhitasthitiḥ /
yāvad āsīta tāvat tu pūrvoktā eva bhūmayaḥ // [AgMsv_2.87]

plain_english: Those levels come into presence as the sole causes for burning away the intoxication of worldly existence, and so does the divine aggregate of senses that had been overgrown by the firm sense of difference.
sanskrit_cite:
sāṃmukhyaṃ yānti saṃsārasadmadāhaikahetavaḥ /
yaś ca divyo 'kṣasaṃghāto bhedarūḍhitirohitaḥ // [AgMsv_2.88]

plain_english: When that aggregate, whose nature is play that nourishes freedom, remains fruitfully turned inward for even a single moment, then—
sanskrit_cite:
svātantryapoṣakakrīḍāmātropakaraṇātmakaḥ /
yadā nimīlanāvandhyas tiṣṭhaty ekaṃ kṣaṇaṃ tadā // [AgMsv_2.89]

plain_english: Then the universe, melted by the great flame of awareness that has arisen through that door, attains the state of resting in the ocean of supreme bliss.
sanskrit_cite:
taddvāroditasaṃbodhamahājvālāvilāpitam /
viśvam abhyeti paramānandasāgaraśāyitām // [AgMsv_2.90]

plain_english: Resting in the drinking of that savor and satisfying the goddesses of awareness, he soon attains freedom from the fear of death and birth.
sanskrit_cite:
tadrasāpānaviśrāntaḥ saṃviddevīḥ pratarpayan /
acirād eti maraṇajanmatrāsavihīnatām // [AgMsv_2.91]

plain_english: For awareness, having congealed and taken on the form of its own awareness, body, senses, and objects, returns by the proper method—once that state has dissolved—to its own dense body of consciousness.
sanskrit_cite:
āśyānabhāvaṃ hi gatā svasaṃviddehendriyajñeyamayatvam āptā /
yuktyā tu sā prāptavilīnabhāvāt saṃvidghanaṃ svaṃ vapur eva yāti // [AgMsv_2.92]

plain_english: By the very same method through which those whose minds are overpowered by external objects emerge outward, there arises the awareness of Bhairava's bliss.
sanskrit_cite:
yuktyā yayaiva bāhyārthavivaśīkṛtacetasām /
vyutthitir jāyate saiva bhairavānandasaṃvidaḥ // [AgMsv_2.93]

plain_english: By that very method, received through the lineage of the yoginī's mouth, the entry of impurity is shaken off and the state made of consciousness stands firm.
sanskrit_cite:
tayaiva yoginīvaktrasaṃpradāyakramāptayā /
vidhūtakalmaṣāveśā tiṣṭhate cinmayī sthitiḥ // [AgMsv_2.94]

plain_english: When the yogin slightly opens the mouth of awareness, all the inner circles of the senses and channels, resting on that traversal, are activated.
sanskrit_cite:
vaktram īṣad yadā yogī vikāsayati saṃvidaḥ /
sarvā indriyanāḍyantaścakrākramaṇasaṃśrayāḥ // [AgMsv_2.95]

plain_english: Then, because of turning toward consciousness, they suddenly move into an expansion consisting in the absence of difference among grasped objects, even though differences like blue and yellow had appeared.
sanskrit_cite:
tadā vikāsaṃ grāhyārthabhedābhāvamayaṃ haṭhāt /
prayānti cidunmukhatvāt nīlapītādibhedavān // [AgMsv_2.96]

plain_english: The difference in the relation between grasper and grasped is split at once through attainment of the lineage rooted in the yoginī's mouth.
sanskrit_cite:
grāhyagrāhakasaṃbandhabhedaḥ sapadi bhidyate /
yoginīvaktrasaṃrūḍhasaṃpradāyakramāptayā // [AgMsv_2.97]

plain_english: Immediately, by the experience-giving seal, he is wholly sealed and absorbed in direct Bhairava, the consciousness-form that presides over all.
sanskrit_cite:
sadyo 'nubhavadāyinyā mudrayā mudritākhilaḥ /
sarvādhiṣṭhātṛcidrūpasākṣādbhairavatandritaḥ // [AgMsv_2.98]

plain_english: That yogin, filled with wonder, obtains awareness of his own self and remains in a state that does not depart even amid the arising and passing of various objects.
sanskrit_cite:
sa yogī vismayāviṣṭo labhate svātmasaṃvidam /
tattaddṛśyodayāpāyayoge 'py anapayatsthiti // [AgMsv_2.99]

plain_english: Water lying low in a tank does not flow elsewhere, even with effort, because it is incapable of doing more than filling that place alone.
sanskrit_cite:
taḍāgavartinimnāmbu tannānyatra pravartate /
prayatnenāpi tanmātrapūraṇāya yad akṣamam // [AgMsv_2.100]

plain_english: But when it is filled with savor by a stream of water flowing through the inner door, then streams filled by that overflow in all directions.
sanskrit_cite:
yadā tvantaḥdvāravāridhārasaṃpūritaṃ rasāt /
bhaved bhaveyustatpūrṇāḥ pravāhāḥ sarvatomukhāḥ // [AgMsv_2.101]

plain_english: Thus, by the force of its own surge, consciousness opens forth by itself and, without division, makes the portions of beings shine as non-different from its own self.
sanskrit_cite:
evaṃ svollāsarabhasāc caitanyaṃ pronmiṣatsvayaṃ /
avibhāgena bhāvāṃśān svātmābhedena bhāsayan // [AgMsv_2.102]

plain_english: If, even for a moment, it does not sink into closure, then through the dissolving of māyā the level of Bhairava shines forth.
sanskrit_cite:
mīlanāviṣayībhāvaṃ śrayed yadi muhūrtakaṃ /
māyāvigalanād bhūmir bhairavīyā virājate // [AgMsv_2.103]

plain_english: For the limitation born of conceptualization may afterward show division; that very division is māyā, the power of the free one that reveals the vision of difference.
sanskrit_cite:
vaikalpiko 'hyavacchedaḥ paścād yāṃ darśayed bhidām /
saiva māyā svatantrasya bhedadṛṣṭiprakāśinī // [AgMsv_2.104]

plain_english: For one who rests only in the opening of consciousness, that māyā is rootless and cannot arise; so what is the use of saying more in this method of the unsurpassed self?
sanskrit_cite:
unmeṣamātrarūḍhasya sā nirmūlā na saṃbhavet /
itthaṃ kiṃ bahunoktena naye 'nuttarātmani // [AgMsv_2.105]

plain_english: In reality, no limb of yoga can serve as a means, for its own nature is formless, being free from all limitation.
sanskrit_cite:
vastuto 'sti na kasyāpi yogāṅgasyābhyupāyatā /
svarūpaṃ hyasya nīrūpam avacchedavivarjanāt // [AgMsv_2.106]

plain_english: Even the means is not a means, because it stops effortful activity; it is free from exhalation and inhalation and from the regulation of body and breath.
sanskrit_cite:
upāya 'pyanupāyo 'syāyāgavṛttinirodhataḥ /
recanapūraṇair eṣā rahitā tanuvātanauḥ // [AgMsv_2.107]

plain_english: Thus this mind carries the self across from the ocean of difference, even when it is sinking while still in the taste of objects.
sanskrit_cite:
tārayaty evam ātmānaṃ bhedasāgaragocarāt /
nimajjamānam apy etan mano vaiṣayike rase // [AgMsv_2.108]

plain_english: A gourd without holes does not become soft inside; likewise, those who forcibly restrain the mind's own path, as if holding back a horse, do not make it inwardly receptive.
sanskrit_cite:
nāntarārdratvam abhyeti niśchidraṃ tumbakaṃ yathā /
svaṃ panthānaṃ hayasyeva manaso ye nirundhate // [AgMsv_2.109]

plain_english: For those who try to break the mind, it runs off along countless wrong paths; wondering, 'What is this?', the mind mostly keeps longing restlessly, even in pain.
sanskrit_cite:
teṣāṃ tatkhaṇḍanayogād dhavaty unmārgakoṭibhiḥ /
kiṃsvid etad iti prāyo duḥkhe 'py utkaṇṭhate manaḥ // [AgMsv_2.110]

plain_english: Through knowledge one can become dispassionate even toward pleasure, discerning 'this is this'; for the teacher has taught this in many ways in his own scripture.
sanskrit_cite:
sukhād api virajyeta jñānād etad idaṃ [tv iti] /
tathāhi gurur ādikṣad bahudhā svakaśāsane // [AgMsv_2.111]

plain_english: The activities of the senses fall away through indifference and dispassion alone; but as long as they are forcibly controlled, they keep acting turbulently.
sanskrit_cite:
anādaraviraktyaiva galantīndriyavṛttayaḥ /
yāvat tu viniyamyante tāvat tāvad vikurvate // [AgMsv_2.112]

plain_english: Even that so-called withdrawal which is applied to the net of the senses becomes, for one whose bondage is already firmly set, a binding as hard as diamond cement.
sanskrit_cite:
pratyāhāro 'pi nāmāyaṃ yo 'kṣajāle pravartyate /
bandhasyārūḍhavṛttes tad vajralepena bandhanam // [AgMsv_2.113]

plain_english: Amid objects, their enjoyment, and the pleasure or pain that arises from them, those whose fear has dissolved, though their minds are immersed, do not truly enter into them and know within the ease of the quieting of mental activity.
sanskrit_cite:
artheṣu tadbhogavidhau tadutthe \ \ duḥkhe sukhe vā galitābhiśaṅkam /
anāviśanto 'pi nimagnacittā \ \ jānanti vṛttikṣayasaukhyam antaḥ // [AgMsv_2.114]

plain_english: When the self, the great light of consciousness, is present in the heart, and the senses and objects such as taste are also present and active, the yogi abides very clearly in a fullness whose arising is free of difference; let that reality be accepted.
sanskrit_cite:
saty evātmani citsvabhāvamahasi svānte tathopakriyāṃ tasmai kurvati tatpracāracature saty akṣavarge 'pi ca /
satsv artheṣu rasādiṣu sphuṭataraṃ yad bhedavandhyodayaṃ yogī tiṣṭhati pūrṇaraśmikhacitas tat tattvam ādīyatām // [AgMsv_2.115]

plain_english: To say that non-discrimination is supreme bondage is only a common saying; for non-discrimination itself can be the supreme stairway to attaining liberation.
sanskrit_cite:
aviveka eva param iha saṃsāra iti pravādamātram /
aviveka eva hi paraṃ niḥśreyasalābhasopānam // [AgMsv_2.116]

plain_english: Abandon deliberate concentrations; where, indeed, would you place concentration? Examine it yourself: in the full it is not fitting, and in the not-full it does not attain true being.
sanskrit_cite:
tyajāvadhānāni nanu kva nāma dhatse 'vadhānaṃ vicinu svayaṃ tat /
pūrṇe 'vadhānaṃ nahi nāma yuktaṃ nāpūrṇam abhyeti ca satyabhāvam // [AgMsv_2.117]

plain_english: Wherever union with bliss arises, there one's own nature is full; if the delusion of difference is understood, one may reach peace there. Even in waking and in every state, the yogi can become the lord of the great wheel of consciousness, moving through varied activities while shining with mantra power.
sanskrit_cite:
yatraivānandayogaḥ kvacana nanu bhavet tatra pūrṇaḥ svabhāvaḥ --- --- te veti tatra praśamapadam iyād yady ayaṃ bhedamohaḥ /
tajjñāne jāgradādāv api nikhilapade cinmahācakranātho yogī jāyeta nānāvyavahṛtapathago 'pyullasan mantravīryaḥ // [AgMsv_2.118]

plain_english: Just as one who sets out to dig a well feels accomplished only when water is reached, while another is satisfied with water already in hand, so the way of attaining the supreme is varied.
sanskrit_cite:
yathā hi kūpaṃ pracikīrṣur eva prāpte jale yāti kṛtitvam ekaḥ /
kaścit punar hastagatādi[vāri]mātrād itthaṃ paraprāptividhir vicitraḥ // [AgMsv_2.119]

plain_english: This is without means; so how, by the usual relation of means and goal, or in any other way, could a person be freed from the bondage of difference?
sanskrit_cite:
anupāyam idaṃ tasmād upāyopeyayogataḥ /
bhedabandhād vimucyeta kathaṃ vetarathā janaḥ // [AgMsv_2.120]

plain_english: Even though this reality is without means, this scripture teaches means in many ways, functioning through relational instruction.
sanskrit_cite:
anupāye 'pi caitasmin kiṃcit sāṃbandhyavṛttitaḥ /
upāyasyopadeśo 'yaṃ śāstre 'tra bahudhā kṛtaḥ // [AgMsv_2.121]

plain_english: Just as children are clearly led into the real nature of sound through written letters, so the deluded are gradually led by those provisional means.
sanskrit_cite:
yathā lipyakṣarair bālāḥ satye varṇātmani sphuṭam /
praveśyante tathā mūḍhais tair aupāyikaiḥ kramāt // [AgMsv_2.122]

plain_english: For that very purpose, even in the nondual supreme reality, this scripture respectfully teaches something appropriate, such as worship and meditation.
sanskrit_cite:
tadartham eva cādvaite paratattve 'pi sādaram /
pūjādhyānādi śāstre 'sminn ucitaṃ kiṃcid ucyate // [AgMsv_2.123]

plain_english: Whatever delights the mind, in any state of the senses, can be joined to the abode of true awareness, to the very opening of Brahman.
sanskrit_cite:
yat kiṃcin manasāhlādi yatra kvāpīndriyasthitau /
yojyate bodhasadbrahmadhāmni brahmabilātmani // [AgMsv_2.124]

plain_english: Resting on absorption in true being that follows the self, one naturally and without effort comes to function as an instrument in the worship of the wheel of the supreme Kula lord and his powers.
sanskrit_cite:
ātmānusārisadbhāvasamāveśadaśāśrayāt

tattatparakuleśānaśakticakrārcanākrame /
prayāty evāprayatnena karaṇatvaṃ svabhāvataḥ // [AgMsv_2.125]

plain_english: Having made the support-ground cleansed by a moment of sprinkling with the essence of wonder, I worship you, O God, together with the Goddess day and night in the temple of the body, using flowers of my own nature taken from the mind and filled with their own fragrance, through the method of the priceless offering-vessel of my own heart overflowing with the nectar of bliss.
sanskrit_cite:
kṛtvādhāradharāṃ camatkṛtirasaprokṣākṣaṇakṣālitām āttair mānasataḥ svabhāvakusumaiḥ svāmodasaṃdohibhiḥ /
ānandāmṛtanirbharasvahṛdayānarghārghapātrakramāt tvāṃ devyā saha dehadevasadane devārcaye 'harniśam // [AgMsv_2.126]

plain_english: Thus, wherever one may stand, by the very nature of one's own reflective awareness, there the entry of the three powers shines forth in a threefold way.
sanskrit_cite:
evaṃ yatra kvacit tiṣṭhet svavimarśasvabhāvataḥ /
tatra śaktitrayāveśas tridhā tāvat prakāśate // [AgMsv_2.127]

plain_english: When that shining appears ninefold, arising from the stated twelve wheels, its repose occurs in a single moment and takes the form of a state numbering one hundred and eight.
sanskrit_cite:
navadhā bhāsamānasya proktadvādaśacakrataḥ /
viśrāntir ekakṣaṇagā sāṣṭottaraśatasthitiḥ // [AgMsv_2.128]

plain_english: That state is clearly discerned as one alone, numbering a hundred; and in this way, whatever speech at all may arise from this yogin belongs to that same state.
sanskrit_cite:
ekaiva śatasaṃkhyā ca sā sthitiḥ pravibhāvyate /
itthaṃ yat kiṃcanaitasya vacanaṃ yogino bhavet // [AgMsv_2.129]

plain_english: That very speech becomes mantra practice on the unsurpassed path, constantly and without any need to rely on the presence of inner fuel.
sanskrit_cite:
tad eva japayogāya jāyate 'nuttare pathi /
antarindhanasadbhāvam anapekṣyaiva nityaśaḥ // [AgMsv_2.130]

plain_english: If one reflectively understands that all beings enter into that which blazes with hundreds of foremost flames spreading forth from all the streams of the senses, then that very place is where their entry occurs.
sanskrit_cite:
yo jvalaty akhilākṣaughaprasṛtāgraśikhāśataḥ /
tatraiva sarvabhāvānāṃ praveśaś ced vimṛśyate // [AgMsv_2.131]
